speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry what considerations do the Singapore Tourism Board give when deciding which artiste or event to disburse grants to.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Aside from leisure events, STB also supports the development and marketing of new tourism products, rejuvenation of existing tourism offerings, upskilling of our tourism workers and also helping our local tourism companies become more productive and innovative.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These events are expected to create value by generating more business for our companies here, adding to Singapore's vibrancy and also amplifying Singapore's global brand and international stature.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: STB tracks overall international visitor arrivals, tourism receipts and the average length of stay.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Members can refer to STB's press release on 1 February 2024 for our tourism sector's performance in 2023.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Considering that other countries in the region are also strengthening their tourism sectors, may I ask, how does our Government maintain our competitiveness and strengthen our tourism competitiveness or proposition?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As Mr Don Wee had mentioned: the other governments, other places, other jurisdictions are not standing still.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We will certainly be lightning on our feet.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And, of course, "haters gonna hate, hate, hate, hate, hate".

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But I am wondering to the extent that STB will work with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or other agencies, to manage this potential fallout when it comes to international relations, and I had previously spoken about the possibility of foreign aid agencies building up soft power, I am wondering if there is any other efforts by STB or any of the MTI agencies in pushing forward this aspect?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But if you think about this, if you take a step back, when visitors come from outside of the region and they come to Singapore, there are also attendant benefits because then they may go and visit other tourist sites around the region.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It is a hub, a hive of activity.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Connectivity helps and it also supports and benefits our neighbours around the region.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we do what is best for Singapore, but we also understand that Singapore is a hub, a connectivity hub, and being a vibrant hub also benefits our region and our neighbours as well.
